source_excerpt:
Greysun is a Senior Editor (Guides) at GameRant, where he oversees game help coverage for everything from the biggest AAA releases to standout indie and live-service titles.
Professionally, Greysun has been writing and editing video game content for over a decade. Before joining GameRant, he spent over four years at Twinfinite, where he worked his way up from Contributing Writer to News Reporter and, ultimately, Features Editor. During that time, he covered major industry news, reviews, guides, and opinion pieces, edited dozens of articles each week, and helped shape the site's content strategy. He has also attended major gaming events such as E3 and PAX, interviewing developers, covering breaking news, and writing opinion pieces on unreleased titles.
Since joining GameRant in 2021, Greysun has served as Lead Guides Editor, planning and managing guide coverage across major releases, coordinating with freelancers, maintaining editorial standards, and writing dozens of articles each month.
A lifelong Nintendo fan since the SNES era, Greysun has a particular soft spot for platformers, JRPGs, and action games that reward curiosity and exploration. He is still patiently awaiting a true sequel to Super Mario Odyssey .
To clean all the Lunar Dust off the moon in Moon Sweepers , you'll start off with a measly toothbrush, but as you gain more currency, you'll slowly get access to more useful tools, such as a Hand Brush, a Household Broom, and even a Tool Belt that lets you carry up to six tools at a time.
This Moon Sweepers guide shows every Tool and gear type you can unlock , plus how much each upgrade costs and when it becomes available.
All Supply Wall Items in Moon Sweepers and How to Get Them
Where everyone starts: slow, but it reaches into every corner.
A little wider than the toothbrush, still made for fine work.
Hand Brush (Unlocks after buying the Nail Brush)
A palm-sized brush for patches, edges, and steps.
Household Broom (Unlocks after buying the Hand Brush)
A proper broom: a lane a stride wide with every sweep.
Building Tool (Unlocks after buying Household Broom)
Builds, moves, and takes down structures. With it in hand, open the build menu.
Wide Broom (Unlocks after buying Building Tool)
Extra Wide Broom (Unlocks after buying Wide Broom)
The widest broom there is: long lanes in one pass.
Tool Belt (price goes up for each slot upgrade)
Another quick slot on your belt: carry one more tool at hand. You start with one slot and can have six.
Helmet Lamp (price goes up for each upgrade)
A better lamp on your helmet: brighter, whiter, wider, further and steady. You start with the suit's flickering surplus lamp.
Gravity Boots (Unlocks after buying first Tool Belt upgrade)
Boots that pull you down as hard as Earth does: low hops, quick landings, and sure footing. Switch them on and off any time.
Forward Jetpack (Unlocks after buying Gravity Boots)
A thruster pack on your back. Jump, then press jump again in the air to burst forward. Boosts refill on the ground; each upgrade adds one.
Night Vision Goggles (Unlocks after buying the Forward Jetpack)
Goggles that light up the lunar night like day so you can see the ground and your base far past the lamp's beam. The helmet lamps key goes round lamp, goggles and off.
